query: For titanium alloys used as structural materials, formulate one hypothesis for an intervention that could increase surface hardness and wear resistance. Specify the intervention, its proposed mechanism, the expected improvement relative to the untreated alloy, the service or test conditions under which the effect should hold, prior evidence supporting the hypothesis, and a controlled experiment with clear results that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: Laser cladding a Ni-doped TiAlCu coating onto a TC4 titanium alloy surface will enhance its surface hardness and wear resistance by promoting the formation of a Ni‐strengthened Ti(Al,Cu)2 phase.
generation.material_initial_state: Standard TC4 titanium alloy substrate with its native microstructure and relatively lower hardness compared to advanced cladding coatings.
generation.intervention: Apply laser cladding using a powder blend of Ti, Al, Cu with added Ni onto the TC4 surface.
generation.conditions: Dry sliding wear tests under loads of 10 N and 30 N at room temperature, simulating service conditions where improved wear behavior is critical.
generation.structural_mediator: The formation of a multiphase coating in which the Ti(Al,Cu)2 phase is modified by Ni inclusion, leading to increased lattice distortion and improved interfacial bonding between phases.
generation.mechanism: Ni atoms dissolve into the Ti(Al,Cu)2 phase, creating a solid solution that increases lattice stress and hinders dislocation movement, while also promoting grain boundary strengthening. These factors collectively increase the coating’s hardness and wear resistance.
generation.predicted_outcome: The Ni-doped cladding should exhibit a maximum hardness around 627.5 HV0.2 (or a similarly significant improvement over the untreated substrate) with reduced friction coefficients and smaller wear track dimensions under the specified loads.
generation.baseline: Untreated TC4 titanium alloy, which shows lower hardness values and higher wear volumes under equivalent dry sliding conditions.
generation.boundary: The effect is expected to hold under room temperature and moderate load conditions (10–30 N); performance under extreme temperatures or corrosive environments has not been established.
generation.uncertainty: Exact improvement levels may vary based on cladding parameters and powder composition optimization. The magnitude of enhancement is anticipated but requires precise quantification through experimental trials.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two groups of TC4 samples: one group is coated via laser cladding with the Ni-doped TiAlCu powder mixture, and the control group remains untreated. Subject both groups to standardized dry sliding wear tests under loads of 10 N and 30 N at room temperature. Perform microhardness and wear volume measurements along the coating and substrate.
measurements: Vickers microhardness (HV0.2) across the coated layer, transition zone, and substrate
Friction coefficient during reciprocating wear tests
Wear track dimensions and calculated wear volumes
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the coated samples do not exhibit a statistically significant increase in hardness (e.g., a 20–30% increase over the untreated TC4) and if wear volumes/frequency of wear failures are not significantly lower than those of the control samples, the hypothesis will be considered falsified.

Multi-principal element alloy coatings were created on the TC4 surface using laser cladding techniques. The addition of Cu and Ni to TiAl alloy powders improved the wear resistance and tensile properties of the coatings. The following conclusions were reached:The coating mainly consists of Ti3Al and Ti(Al, Cu)2 phases, with Ni fully dissolved in the Ti(Al, Cu)2 phase and some TiAl phases, resulting in a multiphase structure that effectively balances strength and toughness. A strong interface is observed between the Ti3Al and Ti(Al, Cu)2 phases. At a microscopic level, the incorporation of Ni alters the phase composition of the coating. Ni, a solid solution within the Ti(Al, Cu)2 phase, induces a solid solution hardening effect, which improves the various properties of the coating.Adding Ni to TiAlCu improves the various properties of the coatings through solid solution strengthening. With increasing Ni content, the hardness increases, while wear resistance and mechanical properties initially improve and then decline.
